summary.text: An 8-year-old girl from rural Sindh, Pakistan, developmentally healthy and fully immunized, had swelling behind the left ear for about one and a half months with pain and foul-smelling discharge, then fever, vomiting and headache for about two weeks. She presented to a pediatric emergency department, appeared ill, febrile and tachycardic, with a fluctuant left postauricular swelling and pus in the ear canal.

Emergency incision and drainage was performed and pus grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with negative GeneXpert, acid-fast smear and blood culture. Leukocytosis, anemia and hypoalbuminemia were found. Contrast CT showed pre-mastoid abscess and left transverse and sigmoid sinus thrombosis extending to the jugular vein, and MRI and MRV showed loss of flow void and a filling defect. Fundoscopy showed bilateral papilledema, worse on the right.

Rivaroxaban and systemic antibiotics including ceftriaxone and vancomycin were given. With no satisfactory improvement after 15 days of antibiotics, a left tympanomastoidectomy with canal wall down clearance and meatoplasty was performed 15 days after admission while rivaroxaban continued. The postoperative period had no complications.

After surgery headache and right eye vision improved, papilledema reduced and leukocyte counts fell to 13.4. Sutures and packing were removed on the tenth postoperative day, rivaroxaban 20 mg once daily continued for 3 months, and the authors describe a favorable outcome.

FIGURE 1
(A) Contrast‐enhanced CT scan of the brain showing the right mastoid air cells (arrow) show sclerosis and partial opacification consistent with chronic mastoiditis.
